headline: Android now lets you use ChatGPT or Claude as your default AI assistant
summary: Google's Gemini is no longer the only AI option for your Android device. You can now set ChatGPT or Claude as your default assistant, but with limitations.
details: Android users can now choose between Google Assistant, ChatGPT, or Claude as their default AI assistant. This allows users to leverage the capabilities of their preferred AI model for everyday tasks.

While ChatGPT excels at conversational tasks and general knowledge questions, it struggles with device control and operating other apps. It failed to consistently provide on-screen text responses for tasks like composing messages, requiring users to manually type them out.

Claude offers a more integrated experience, capable of setting alarms, timers, and managing calendar events with user approval. It also boasts connectors for various third-party apps like Gmail, Google Calendar, and productivity suites.

However, Claude is not without its flaws. It cannot perform actions like toggling flashlight, opening apps, or sending texts. Users also need to re-authenticate connections periodically, and occasional transcription errors or voice mode dropouts were reported.

The ability to set third-party AI models as the default assistant marks a significant shift in Android's ecosystem, offering users greater flexibility and choice in how they interact with their devices.

For users who prioritize conversational AI and general knowledge, ChatGPT might be a viable option. However, for those needing more device integration and task management, Claude presents a closer alternative to Gemini, albeit with its own set of limitations.
caption:
Android now lets you ditch Google Assistant for ChatGPT or Claude. But how do they stack up against Gemini?

Android users can now choose between Google Assistant, ChatGPT, or Claude as their default AI assistant. This allows users to leverage the capabilities of their preferred AI model for everyday tasks.

While ChatGPT excels at conversational tasks and general knowledge questions, it struggles with device control and operating other apps. It failed to consistently provide on-screen text responses for tasks like composing messages, requiring users to manually type them out.

Claude offers a more integrated experience, capable of setting alarms, timers, and managing calendar events with user approval. It also boasts connectors for various third-party apps like Gmail, Google Calendar, and productivity suites.

However, Claude is not without its flaws. It cannot perform actions like toggling flashlight, opening apps, or sending texts. Users also need to re-authenticate connections periodically, and occasional transcription errors or voice mode dropouts were reported.

The ability to set third-party AI models as the default assistant marks a significant shift in Android's ecosystem, offering users greater flexibility and choice in how they interact with their devices.

For users who prioritize conversational AI and general knowledge, ChatGPT might be a viable option. However, for those needing more device integration and task management, Claude presents a closer alternative to Gemini, albeit with its own set of limitations.
